horsham.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of West Sussex
s1loc: Horsham keeps a busy events calendar for a West Sussex market town. The Capitol on North Street runs touring drama, live music and two cinema screens, and Horsham Park carries the open-air season: Enchanted Horsham brings three days of music, circus and street food in late summer, the Horsham Fake Festival fills a June day, and the long-running Horsham Battle of the Bands stages its finals in the Human Nature Garden amphitheatre, with heats around rooms like the Holbrook Club.

s1loc: Washington sits in the Sunderland and Tyne and Wear events corridor. Arts Centre Washington on Biddick Lane at Fatfield runs a year-round programme of theatre, music, dance and comedy, with the award-winning Davy Lamp Folk Club in its Low Barn and a recording studio and rehearsal rooms behind the stage, while the Galleries shopping centre hosts seasonal events in the town. Bigger crowds gather a short hop away at Sunderland and Gateshead, with the Stadium of Light and Sage area drawing arena tours.

Washington pairs its arts centre with strong heritage and outdoor sites. Washington Old Hall, the ancestral home of George Washington's family, draws heritage days, the WWT wetlands centre and Princess Anne Park host community events, and Penshaw Monument stands over the area as its landmark. A new town between Sunderland and Gateshead, it keeps crews and front-of-house teams busy across a spread of Wearside and Tyneside dates.
